summary: baseSize is documented as what it is, the type scale's 16px reference, not the body size, and validateSeed now explains a small one. Its JSDoc said "Body size in px. Drives the whole type scale"; a consumer set 13 expecting 13px body and got --ui-text-body-md 11.375px, because baseSize multiplies the authored table (ADR 0009) by baseSize / 16 and body copy is the table's 14px row. SeedTypography.baseSize now carries the mapping table (baseSize to body-lg, body-md, body-sm and label-sm px, 13 to 20) and the inverse (B px body needs baseSize B × 16 / 14). SeedValidationIssue gains a required `severity: "error" | "info"`: every existing issue is `error` (an unusable value the resolver fell back on); a baseSize under BASE_SIZE_INFO_BELOW (15, exported) adds an `info` issue stating the resolved body-md, body-sm and label-sm/caption sizes, that they sit under the scale's 12px floor, and the baseSize that would give the body size the author typed. resolveTheme returns it in `issues` like any other.

migration.manual: Nothing breaks for code that reads issues. Code that treated ANY issue as a failure should now fail only on `severity === "error"` and print `info`. A seed with baseSize under 15 that was chosen expecting that body size: set baseSize to the wanted body px × 16 / 14.
